info.title: GetReal Property API
info.description:
## About this API

GetReal is a free, open data project that helps Australians assess whether their property search is realistic. This API exposes the same calculations powering the GetReal tools — stamp duty, LMI, borrowing ceilings, and suburb realism scores.

## Data sources

- **NSW property sales:** NSW Valuer General bulk PSI data — 146,000+ individual sale records, updated weekly.
- **VIC property sales:** Victorian Valuer General quarterly suburb median reports. VIC scores are estimated using NSW-derived price distribution curves (see [methodology](/faq.html)).
- **Stamp duty:** State Revenue Offices for all 8 states and territories, including 2026 FHB concessions.
- **LMI rates:** Indicative Helia/QBE rates sourced from Home Loan Experts (May 2026).
- **HEM benchmarks:** Indicative Household Expenditure Measure figures sourced from JMD Mortgages (March 2026).
- **RBA benchmark rates:** Reserve Bank of Australia Statistical Tables, updated weekly.

## Important disclaimer

**This API is a best-efforts side project, not a licensed financial service.** Results are indicative only and should not be relied upon as the sole basis for financial decisions. Always verify stamp duty, LMI, and borrowing capacity with a licensed mortgage broker and check current market conditions.

Rate data is updated regularly but may lag real-world changes. Stamp duty rates reflect legislation as of mid-2026 — verify current rates with your state revenue office before transacting.

## Rate limits and cost

This API is free to use. Please be reasonable — batch endpoints exist for multi-suburb queries so you don't need to hammer individual endpoints. If you're building something commercial on top of this, reach out.

## Base URL

`https://get-real.co/api/v1/`

## Authentication

No authentication required. All data is public.

## Request format

All endpoints accept `GET` with query parameters.

## Error format

```json
{ "error": "Human-readable message", "code": "MACHINE_CODE" }
```

Error codes: `MISSING_PARAM`, `INVALID_INPUT`, `SUBURB_NOT_FOUND`, `INSUFFICIENT_SAVINGS`, `NOT_FOUND`, `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

get.description:
Calculates stamp duty for any Australian state and buyer type. Applies FHB concessions and 2026 rates. Includes registration fees.

Data source: state revenue offices. Rates reflect legislation as of mid-2026.

Estimates Lenders Mortgage Insurance (LMI) for a given purchase price and deposit. LMI applies when LVR exceeds 80%.

Rates are indicative Helia/QBE figures sourced from Home Loan Experts (May 2026). Actual LMI varies by lender.

Standard P&I monthly repayment for a given loan amount. Omit `rate_pct` to use the current RBA benchmark rate. Always returns the stress-tested repayment (benchmark + 3%) alongside the actual repayment.

Useful for sanity-checking a loan size before using the full ceiling endpoints.

parameters.name: rate_pct

schema.description: Annual interest rate (%). Omit to use current RBA benchmark rate.

parameters.description: Annual interest rate (%). Omit to use current RBA benchmark rate.

get.description:
Given a savings amount and property context, returns the maximum purchase price the deposit can reach after accounting for stamp duty, LMI, and registration fees.

This answers the 'what can I buy with what I've saved?' question — without needing income details.

The calculation binary-searches for the highest price at which savings cover the required upfront costs and deposit component under the maximum LVR.

parameters.name: savings

schema.description: Total savings available for deposit and upfront costs

parameters.description: Total savings available for deposit and upfront costs

get.description:
Extends the deposit ceiling to also return the minimum gross income (DTI) and minimum net monthly income (serviceability at HEM floor) needed to actually borrow the resulting loan.

Answers 'I know my savings — tell me the max price AND whether I can qualify.'

Returns the maximum new mortgage loan allowed under the 6× DTI rule (per APRA guidelines), accounting for existing debt obligations.

Credit cards are counted at their full limit. Existing investment mortgages are partially offset by rental income (80% of weekly rent × 52). HECS debt is not counted directly but note lenders vary in their treatment.

Returns the maximum loan supportable from take-home pay under the APRA serviceability test (repayment at benchmark + 3% stress rate).

The HEM (Household Expenditure Measure) floor is applied based on household type, dependants, and location. Source: indicative JMD Mortgages figures.

parameters.name: assessment_rate_pct

schema.description: Override assessment rate. Omit to use benchmark + 3%.

parameters.description: Override assessment rate. Omit to use benchmark + 3%.

get.summary: All three ceilings in one call
get.description:
Runs deposit (C1), DTI (C2), and serviceability (C3) ceilings together and identifies the binding constraint (lowest of the three).

This is the complete affordability picture in a single request.

get.summary: Can I afford a target price?
get.description: Given a target price and full financial inputs, returns a yes/no with a breakdown per ceiling showing where any shortfall is and what levers are available to close it.

get.summary: Savings sensitivity — what if I saved more?
get.description: Returns how the deposit ceiling changes at different savings amounts. Shows whether additional saving crosses the 80% LVR threshold (avoiding LMI) and at what point.

get.summary: Score a budget in one suburb
get.description:
Returns the percentage of properties that sold in a suburb at or below a given budget. This is GetReal's core realism score.

**NSW:** Score based on actual Valuer General sale records.

**VIC:** Score estimated from NSW-derived price distribution curves matched by property type, price bracket (5 bands), and market depth (active ≥30 sales/yr, thin <30). Individual sale records are not publicly available in VIC.

Score labels: `very_strong` (≥75), `strong` (≥55), `comfortable` (≥35), `tight` (≥15), `very_tight` (≥5), `out_of_range` (<5).

get.summary: Score a budget across multiple suburbs
get.description: Score a single budget across up to 20 suburbs in one call. Results sorted by score descending. Answers 'where can my budget go furthest?'

get.summary: Budget needed to hit a target score
get.description:
Reverse lookup. Given a suburb and a target score percentile, returns the budget required to reach it.

Answers 'I want to be comfortable in Fitzroy — what do I need to spend?'

get.summary: Which suburbs can I compete in?
get.description:
Returns all suburbs in a state where a given budget scores above a minimum threshold. Sorted by score descending.

Use `min_score_pct` to filter — default 30 (comfortable or better). Use `limit` to cap results — default 20.

get.summary: Score a ceiling against a suburb
get.description:
Runs the full ceiling calculation for a user's situation, then immediately scores that ceiling against a target suburb.

Single call for the end-to-end question: 'Can I actually afford to buy in [suburb] given my financial situation?'

BuyerType.description: fhb = first home buyer, owner = owner-occupier (not FHB), investor = investment purchase

LocationType.description: metro = capital city; regional = rest of state
